info.name: Mess_Tally
info.description:
Postman collection for the MessTally backend. Covers every route currently mounted in the app: `/api/v1/auth`, `/api/v1/mess`, and the root health route.

Base URL is controlled by the `baseUrl` collection variable (default: http://localhost:8000, matching PORT in .env). Login, Verify Email, Refresh Token, and Create Mess save the returned tokens into collection variables and also set the httpOnly cookies. Join Mess stores the joined mess and membership ids in collection variables.

Protected routes accept the access token either from the cookie jar or via the `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` header. `Refresh Token` reads the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie, so it must run after Login, Verify Email, or Create Mess in the same Postman session.

request.description:
Stores the pending registration in Redis and emails a 6-digit OTP (valid for 5 minutes). The user is only created after Verify Email.

In development the OTP is also printed in the server console as `[dev] OTP <email> : <otp>`.

Validates the registration OTP, creates the user, sends the welcome email, and sets `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies.

The test script stores both tokens in collection variables.

Logs in an active, email-verified user and sets `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies.

The test script stores both tokens in collection variables.

Returns the logged-in user's account and profile.

Requires a valid access token, supplied either by the `accessToken` cookie set during Login / Verify Email or by the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

Issues a new access token and refresh token using the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie.

No request body is required, and the controller does not read an Authorization header — run Login, Verify Email, or Create Mess first so Postman has the refresh cookie. The test script updates both collection variables with the new tokens.

Sends a 6-digit password reset OTP to the email (valid for 5 minutes). The OTP is stored in Redis under `user-forgetPassword-otp:<email>`.

Only active, email-verified, non-deleted users can request a reset. In development the OTP is printed in the server console.

Use the received OTP with the Reset Password request.

Verifies the password reset OTP sent by Forgot Password and updates the user's password.

The OTP must match `user-forgetPassword-otp:<email>` in Redis and expires after 5 minutes. It is deleted after a successful reset, so it can only be used once.

A password-reset confirmation email is sent to the user after the password is updated.

Updates the authenticated user's profile information.

At least one of `bio`, `phone`, or `address` is required. All fields are optional and support empty strings for clearing existing values. Requires a valid access token and an active, email-verified account.

The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

Uploads or replaces the authenticated user's profile image.

Send the image as `multipart/form-data` using the `profileImage` field. Only JPEG, PNG, and WebP images are accepted, with a maximum size of 5 MB. The previous Cloudinary image is deleted after a successful replacement.

**Before sending, select an actual image file in the `profileImage` field.** If that field is left empty, Postman fails locally with `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read` and the request never reaches the server. The request method must be `PATCH`.

Requires a valid access token and an active, email-verified account. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Sunrise Mess",
  "address": "House 12, Road 3, Dhanmondi, Dhaka",
  "currency": "BDT",
  "mealCutoffTime": "11:00",
  "isJoinable": true,
  "requireApproval": true
}

request.description:
Creates a mess and makes the logged-in user its OWNER (also flagged as manager and ACTIVE). Protected by `auth()`, so any authenticated user can call it.

Only `name` is required; `address`, `currency`, `mealCutoffTime`, `isJoinable`, and `requireApproval` are optional. Server defaults: `currency` = "BDT", `mealCutoffTime` = "11:00", `isJoinable` = true, `requireApproval` = true.

A user can only be ACTIVE in one mess: if the caller already has an ACTIVE membership, this returns `409 Conflict` and asks them to leave that mess first.

The server pulls the next integer from the `mess_room_code_seq` PostgreSQL sequence and encodes it with Sqids, prefixed by the first three letters of the mess name (e.g. "Sunrise Mess" -> `SUN-JEVTDKRA`). In one transaction it creates the mess, the OWNER membership, and sets `user.activeMessId`.

Responds `201` with `{ mess, activeMessId }`. No tokens or cookies are issued here: tokens are identity-only and come from login/refresh. The test script stores `messId`, `activeMessId`, `roomCode`, and `messName`.

Joins an existing mess using its `roomCode` (case-insensitive, trimmed). Protected by `auth()`, with `validateRequest` enforcing that `roomCode` is present.

Responds `201` with `{ mess, membership, activeMessId }`. The membership is `PENDING` when the mess has `requireApproval = true` (then `activeMessId` is `null`), otherwise `ACTIVE` and `user.activeMessId` is set to this mess.

No tokens are issued here. Errors: `404` unknown room code, `403` when `isJoinable = false`, `409` when the user already has a `PENDING`/`ACTIVE` membership in this mess or is `ACTIVE` in another mess. A previous `LEFT` or `REJECTED` row is reused and reset to `MEMBER` with manager rights cleared.

Run Create Mess first to populate `roomCode`, but use an account that is not ACTIVE in another mess. The test script stores `joinedMessId`, `membershipId`, `membershipStatus`, and `activeMessId`.

Lists every mess the logged-in user belongs to, for the mess picker. Protected by `auth()` only: this endpoint must stay usable when the caller has no active mess, so it never calls `requireActiveMembership`.

Responds `200` with `{ activeMessId, messes[] }`. Each row carries `membershipId`, `role`, `status`, `isManager`, `joinedAt`, `leftAt`, `isActive`, and a `mess` summary (`id`, `name`, `address`, `currency`, `roomCode`, `isJoinable`, `requireApproval`, `mealCutoffTime`).

Rows are `ACTIVE` first, then `PENDING`, then `LEFT` (newest first within each group); `REJECTED` is excluded. `isActive` marks the one mess pointed at by `user.activeMessId`, and `activeMessId` is `null` when that pointer is missing or stale (no matching `ACTIVE` membership), so the token/JWT is never trusted for scope.

The test script asserts the list shape and syncs `activeMessId` (or unsets it when null).

query.description: Optional. Enable to return only rows with this status (PENDING | ACTIVE | LEFT | REJECTED). Leave disabled for the full member list.

request.description:
Lists every `mess_member` row of the caller's active mess (all statuses by default), ordered ACTIVE -> PENDING -> LEFT -> REJECTED. Any ACTIVE member may call it.

The optional `?status=ACTIVE` filter is what the meals, bazar and utility dropdowns use (AC 2.1.2). An invalid status value returns `400`.

Responds `200` with `{ members[], total }`. Each row has `id` (the `mess_member` id used by every other endpoint), `userId`, `name`, `email`, `avatarUrl`, `role`, `status`, `isManager`, `rentShare`, `fixedRentAmount`, `joinedAt`, and `leftAt`.

The test script stores the first ACTIVE non-owner member as `memberId`, which is the target used by Transfer Manager, Transfer Ownership and Remove Member.

Manager only (`is_manager = true`). Lists `PENDING` join requests for the caller's active mess, oldest first.

Responds `200` with `{ members[], total }` in the same shape as List Members. A non-manager gets `403`, and so does a caller without a valid ACTIVE membership.

The test script stores the first request as `pendingMemberId`.

Manager only. Moves a `PENDING` join request to `ACTIVE`, stamps `joinedAt`, and points `user.activeMessId` at this mess (PRD 2.1).

Scoped by mess: a member id from another mess returns `404`; a row that is not `PENDING` returns `409`. Because a user can be ACTIVE in only one mess (D14), approval is also rejected with `409` when the user has become active in another mess in the meantime.

Responds `200` with the updated member row.

Manager only. Moves a `PENDING` join request to `REJECTED` and clears `isManager`. The row is kept (D10) so a later join reuses it; rejected rows are excluded from all calculations and dropdowns.

`404` when the id is not in the caller's mess, `409` when the row is not `PENDING`. Responds `200` with the updated member row.

Transfers the manager position to the target ACTIVE member. The caller gives up `is_manager` and the target receives it, so a mess never has more than one manager. A manager can hand the position to another member; if the caller is the OWNER, `role` stays `OWNER` and only the manager flag moves. The OWNER can also call this when they no longer hold the flag, so a mess can never be stuck without a manager (for example after a manager leaves). Ownership itself is a separate action: `PATCH /api/mess/members/:id/owner`.

No request body is needed. The target must be an ACTIVE member of the caller's mess and cannot be the caller (`400`). Plain members get `403`, unknown or cross-mess ids `404`, non-active targets `409`. Responds `200` with the target row (`isManager: true`); refetch `GET /api/mess/members` to see the previous manager's row as `false`.

exec: pm.test("exactly one OWNER and one manager remain", () => {

request.description:
OWNER only. Moves the OWNER role to an ACTIVE member of the same mess: the target becomes `OWNER` with `isManager: true`, and the previous owner becomes a `MEMBER` with `isManager: false`, so exactly one owner and one manager remain. The current owner is demoted before the target is promoted so the `mess_member_one_owner_idx` partial unique index is never violated.

Run this before `POST /api/mess/leave` when the mess still has other active members; leaving as the owner returns `409` until ownership is transferred. The target must be ACTIVE, in the same mess, and not the caller (`400`). A non-owner caller gets `403`, unknown or cross-mess ids `404`, non-active targets `409`. Responds `200` with the new owner's member row.

Leaves the caller's active mess: sets `status = LEFT`, stamps `leftAt`, clears `isManager`, and nulls `user.activeMessId`. Switching messes means leaving and then joining another (D7).

An OWNER with other ACTIVE members must first transfer ownership with `PATCH /api/mess/members/:id/owner` (`409` otherwise); the last active member can always leave. Responds `200` with `{ messId, leftAt, activeMessId: null }`.

Manager only hard delete, reserved for members with no records at all (AC 2.1.3). Blocked with `409` when meal entries, bazar, deposits, utility bills or payments reference the member; the message lists the counts and suggests setting `status = LEFT` instead (D12).

The owner cannot be removed (`403`) and a manager cannot remove themselves (`400`, use Leave). A member id from another mess returns `404`. Responds `200` with `{ id, deleted: true }`.
Basic health/welcome route. Returns `{ success: true, message: "Welcome to MessTally" }`.
